headline: Single-cell computational methods infer regulators, trajectories and tumor lineages
label: Computational Omics Method Frameworks
summary: Longitudinal, multimodal and lineage-barcoded single-cell datasets are now paired with inference methods that model dynamics and regulation directly.
synthesis: The dominant thread is that experimental design features, including sister-cell lineage barcodes, recombination barcodes and longitudinal sampling, are built into inference rather than handled as post hoc corrections. TwINFER uses sister-cell twin information to resolve the direction and type of gene regulatory interactions, and DemuxHMM couples recombination barcodes with a hidden Markov model to demultiplex pooled embryo scRNA-seq. Optimal transport fate mapping reconstructs continuous CD8 T cell trajectories across time and tissues, and CellPace uses gap-aware time encodings within a diffusion model for irregularly sampled dynamics. Other items extend this principle to graph contrastive learning, biclustering, multi-donor demultiplexing and tumor phylogeny inference from low-pass scDNA-seq. What is new is the integration of experimental structure into the model itself, although the set is heterogeneous and not every item shares this design.
